units.leftText: In the days when the judges judged, there was a famine in the land. A certain man of Bethlehem Judah went to live in the country of Moab with his wife and his two sons.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the days when the judges judged, that there was a famine in the land. And a certain man of Beth-lehem-judah went to sojourn in the country of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.

units.leftText: The name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi. The names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehem Judah. They came into the country of Moab and lived there.
units.rightText: And the name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi, and the name of his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Beth-lehem-judah. And they came into the country of Moab, and continued there.

units.leftText: Elimelech, Naomi’s husband, died; and she was left with her two sons.
units.rightText: And Elimelech, Naomi’s husband, died; and she was left, and her two sons.

units.leftText: They took for themselves wives of the women of Moab. The name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other was Ruth. They lived there about ten years.
units.rightText: And they took them wives of the women of Moab; the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other Ruth: and they dwelt there about ten years.

units.leftText: Mahlon and Chilion both died, and the woman was bereaved of her two children and of her husband.
units.rightText: And Mahlon and Chilion died both of them; and the woman was left of her two children and of her husband.

units.leftText: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law, that she might return from the country of Moab; for she had heard in the country of Moab how the LORD had visited his people in giving them bread.
units.rightText: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law, that she might return from the country of Moab: for she had heard in the country of Moab how that Jehovah had visited his people in giving them bread.
leftNotes: 1:6 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: She went out of the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her. They went on the way to return to the land of Judah.
units.rightText: And she went forth out of the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her; and they went on the way to return unto the land of Judah.

units.leftText: Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return each of you to her mother’s house. May the LORD deal kindly with you, as you have dealt with the dead and with me.
units.rightText: And Naomi said unto her two daughters-in-law, Go, return each of you to her mother’s house: Jehovah deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead, and with me.

units.leftText: May the LORD grant you that you may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband.”
units.rightText: Jehovah grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband. Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voice, and wept.

units.leftText: They said to her, “No, but we will return with you to your people.”
units.rightText: And they said unto her, Nay, but we will return with thee unto thy people.

units.leftText: Naomi said, “Go back, my daughters. Why do you want to go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?
units.rightText: And Naomi said, Turn again, my daughters: why will ye go with me? have I yet sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?

units.leftText: Go back, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say, ‘I have hope,’ if I should even have a husband tonight, and should also bear sons,
units.rightText: Turn again, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say, I have hope, if I should even have a husband to-night, and should also bear sons;

units.leftText: would you then wait until they were grown? Would you then refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters, for it grieves me seriously for your sakes, for the LORD’s hand has gone out against me.”
units.rightText: would ye therefore tarry till they were grown? would ye therefore stay from having husbands? nay, my daughters, for it grieveth me much for your sakes, for the hand of Jehovah is gone forth against me.

units.leftText: They lifted up their voices and wept again; then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth stayed with her.
units.rightText: And they lifted up their voice, and wept again: and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clave unto her.

units.leftText: She said, “Behold, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her god. Follow your sister-in-law.”
units.rightText: And she said, Behold, thy sister-in-law is gone back unto her people, and unto her god: return thou after thy sister-in-law.
leftNotes: 1:15 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Ruth said, “Don’t urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.
units.rightText: And Ruth said, Entreat me not to leave thee, and to return from following after thee, for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God;

units.leftText: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD do so to me, and more also, if anything but death parts you and me.”
units.rightText: where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried: Jehovah do so to me, and more also, if aught but death part thee and me.

units.leftText: When Naomi saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her.
units.rightText: And when she saw that she was stedfastly minded to go with her, she left off speaking unto her.

units.leftText: So they both went until they came to Bethlehem. When they had come to Bethlehem, all the city was excited about them, and they asked, “Is this Naomi?”
units.rightText: So they two went until they came to Beth-lehem. And it came to pass, when they were come to Beth-lehem, that all the city was moved about them, and the women said, Is this Naomi?

units.leftText: She said to them, “Don’t call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
units.rightText: And she said unto them, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara; for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.

units.leftText: I went out full, and the LORD has brought me home again empty. Why do you call me Naomi, since the LORD has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me?”
units.rightText: I went out full, and Jehovah hath brought me home again empty; why call ye me Naomi, seeing Jehovah hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me?

units.leftText: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, with her, who returned out of the country of Moab. They came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.
units.rightText: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, with her, who returned out of the country of Moab: and they came to Beth-lehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

units.leftText: Naomi had a relative of her husband’s, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.
units.rightText: And Naomi had a kinsman of her husband’s, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.

units.leftText: Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, “Let me now go to the field, and glean among the ears of grain after him in whose sight I find favor.”
units.rightText: And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and glean among the ears of grain after him in whose sight I shall find favor. And she said unto her, Go, my daughter.

units.leftText: She went, and came and gleaned in the field after the reapers; and she happened to come to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech.
units.rightText: And she went, and came and gleaned in the field after the reapers: and her hap was to light on the portion of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech.

units.leftText: Behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said to the reapers, “May the LORD be with you.”
units.rightText: And, behold, Boaz came from Beth-lehem, and said unto the reapers, Jehovah be with you. And they answered him, Jehovah bless thee.

units.leftText: Then Boaz said to his servant who was set over the reapers, “Whose young lady is this?”
units.rightText: Then said Boaz unto his servant that was set over the reapers, Whose damsel is this?

units.leftText: The servant who was set over the reapers answered, “It is the Moabite lady who came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab.
units.rightText: And the servant that was set over the reapers answered and said, It is the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab:

units.leftText: She said, ‘Please let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves.’ So she came, and has continued even from the morning until now, except that she rested a little in the house.”
units.rightText: and she said, Let me glean, I pray you, and gather after the reapers among the sheaves. So she came, and hath continued even from the morning until now, save that she tarried a little in the house.

units.leftText: Then Boaz said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Don’t go to glean in another field, and don’t go from here, but stay here close to my maidens.
units.rightText: Then said Boaz unto Ruth, Hearest thou not, my daughter? Go not to glean in another field, neither pass from hence, but abide here fast by my maidens.

units.leftText: Let your eyes be on the field that they reap, and go after them. Haven’t I commanded the young men not to touch you? When you are thirsty, go to the vessels, and drink from that which the young men have drawn.”
units.rightText: Let thine eyes be on the field that they do reap, and go thou after them: have I not charged the young men that they shall not touch thee? and when thou art athirst, go unto the vessels, and drink of that which the young men have drawn.

units.leftText: Then she fell on her face and bowed herself to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found favor in your sight, that you should take knowledge of me, since I am a foreigner?”
units.rightText: Then she fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground, and said unto him, Why have I found favor in thy sight, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a foreigner?

units.leftText: Boaz answered her, “I have been told all about what you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, and how you have left your father, your mother, and the land of your birth, and have come to a people that you didn’t know before.
units.rightText: And Boaz answered and said unto her, It hath fully been showed me, all that thou hast done unto thy mother-in-law since the death of thy husband; and how thou hast left thy father and thy mother, and the land of thy nativity, and art come unto a people that thou knewest not heretofore.

units.leftText: May the LORD repay your work, and a full reward be given to you from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.”
units.rightText: Jehovah recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of Jehovah, the God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to take refuge.

units.leftText: Then she said, “Let me find favor in your sight, my lord, because you have comforted me, and because you have spoken kindly to your servant, though I am not as one of your servants.”
units.rightText: Then she said, Let me find favor in thy sight, my lord, for that thou hast comforted me, and for that thou hast spoken kindly unto thy handmaid, though I be not as one of thy handmaidens.

units.leftText: At meal time Boaz said to her, “Come here, and eat some bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar.”
units.rightText: And at meal-time Boaz said unto her, Come hither, and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the vinegar. And she sat beside the reapers, and they reached her parched grain, and she did eat, and was sufficed, and left thereof.

units.leftText: When she had risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and don’t reproach her.
units.rightText: And when she was risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, Let her glean even among the sheaves, and reproach her not.

units.leftText: Also pull out some for her from the bundles, and leave it. Let her glean, and don’t rebuke her.”
units.rightText: And also pull out some for her from the bundles, and leave it, and let her glean, and rebuke her not.

units.leftText: So she gleaned in the field until evening; and she beat out that which she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.
units.rightText: So she gleaned in the field until even; and she beat out that which she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.
leftNotes: 2:17 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel

units.leftText: She took it up, and went into the city. Then her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned; and she brought out and gave to her that which she had left after she had enough.
units.rightText: And she took it up, and went into the city; and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned: and she brought forth and gave to her that which she had left after she was sufficed.

units.leftText: Her mother-in-law said to her, “Where have you gleaned today? Where have you worked? Blessed be he who noticed you.”
units.rightText: And her mother-in-law said unto her, Where hast thou gleaned to-day? and where hast thou wrought? blessed be he that did take knowledge of thee. And she showed her mother-in-law with whom she had wrought, and said, The man’s name with whom I wrought to-day is Boaz.

units.leftText: Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the LORD, who has not abandoned his kindness to the living and to the dead.” Naomi said to her, “The man is a close relative to us, one of our near kinsmen.”
units.rightText: And Naomi said unto her daughter-in-law, Blessed be he of Jehovah, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead. And Naomi said unto her, The man is nigh of kin unto us, one of our near kinsmen.

units.leftText: Ruth the Moabitess said, “Yes, he said to me, ‘You shall stay close to my young men until they have finished all my harvest.’”
units.rightText: And Ruth the Moabitess said, Yea, he said unto me, Thou shalt keep fast by my young men, until they have ended all my harvest.

units.leftText: Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his maidens, and that they not harm you in any other field.”
units.rightText: And Naomi said unto Ruth her daughter-in-law, It is good, my daughter, that thou go out with his maidens, and that they meet thee not in any other field.

units.leftText: So she stayed close to the maidens of Boaz, to glean to the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest; and she lived with her mother-in-law.
units.rightText: So she kept fast by the maidens of Boaz, to glean unto the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest; and she dwelt with her mother-in-law.

units.leftText: Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, “My daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?
units.rightText: And Naomi her mother-in-law said unto her, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee?

units.leftText: Now isn’t Boaz our kinsman, with whose maidens you were? Behold, he will be winnowing barley tonight on the threshing floor.
units.rightText: And now is not Boaz our kinsman, with whose maidens thou wast? Behold, he winnoweth barley to-night in the threshing-floor.

units.leftText: Therefore wash yourself, anoint yourself, get dressed, and go down to the threshing floor; but don’t make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
units.rightText: Wash thyself therefore, and anoint thee, and put thy raiment upon thee, and get thee down to the threshing-floor, but make not thyself known unto the man, until he shall have done eating and drinking.

units.leftText: It shall be, when he lies down, that you shall note the place where he is lying. Then you shall go in, uncover his feet, and lie down. Then he will tell you what to do.”
units.rightText: And it shall be, when he lieth down, that thou shalt mark the place where he shall lie, and thou shalt go in, and uncover his feet, and lay thee down; and he will tell thee what thou shalt do.

units.leftText: She said to her, “All that you say, I will do.”
units.rightText: And she said unto her, All that thou sayest I will do.

units.leftText: She went down to the threshing floor, and did everything that her mother-in-law told her.
units.rightText: And she went down unto the threshing-floor, and did according to all that her mother-in-law bade her.

units.leftText: When Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. She came softly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
units.rightText: And when Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain: and she came softly, and uncovered his feet, and laid her down.

units.leftText: At midnight, the man was startled and turned himself; and behold, a woman lay at his feet.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was afraid, and turned himself; and, behold, a woman lay at his feet.

units.leftText: He said, “Who are you?”
units.rightText: And he said, Who art thou? And she answered, I am Ruth thy handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thy handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.

units.leftText: He said, “You are blessed by the LORD, my daughter. You have shown more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, because you didn’t follow young men, whether poor or rich.
units.rightText: And he said, Blessed be thou of Jehovah, my daughter: thou hast showed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich.

units.leftText: Now, my daughter, don’t be afraid. I will do to you all that you say; for all the city of my people knows that you are a worthy woman.
units.rightText: And now, my daughter, fear not; I will do to thee all that thou sayest; for all the city of my people doth know that thou art a worthy woman.

units.leftText: Now it is true that I am a near kinsman. However, there is a kinsman nearer than I.
units.rightText: And now it is true that I am a near kinsman; howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I.

units.leftText: Stay this night, and in the morning, if he will perform for you the part of a kinsman, good. Let him do the kinsman’s duty. But if he will not do the duty of a kinsman for you, then I will do the duty of a kinsman for you, as the LORD lives. Lie down until the morning.”
units.rightText: Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman’s part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to thee, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee, as Jehovah liveth: lie down until the morning.

units.leftText: She lay at his feet until the morning, then she rose up before one could discern another. For he said, “Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor.”
units.rightText: And she lay at his feet until the morning: and she rose up before one could discern another. For he said, Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing-floor.

units.leftText: He said, “Bring the mantle that is on you, and hold it.” She held it; and he measured six measures of barley, and laid it on her; then he went into the city.
units.rightText: And he said, Bring the mantle that is upon thee, and hold it; and she held it; and he measured six measures of barley, and laid it on her: and he went into the city.

units.leftText: When she came to her mother-in-law, she said, “How did it go, my daughter?”
units.rightText: And when she came to her mother-in-law, she said, Who art thou, my daughter? And she told her all that the man had done to her.

units.leftText: She said, “He gave me these six measures of barley; for he said, ‘Don’t go empty to your mother-in-law.’”
units.rightText: And she said, These six measures of barley gave he me; for he said, Go not empty unto thy mother-in-law.

units.leftText: Then she said, “Wait, my daughter, until you know what will happen; for the man will not rest until he has settled this today.”
units.rightText: Then said she, Sit still, my daughter, until thou know how the matter will fall; for the man will not rest, until he have finished the thing this day.

units.leftText: Now Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there. Behold, the near kinsman of whom Boaz spoke came by. Boaz said to him, “Come over here, friend, and sit down!” He came over, and sat down.
units.rightText: Now Boaz went up to the gate, and sat him down there: and, behold, the near kinsman of whom Boaz spake came by; unto whom he said, Ho, such a one! turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside, and sat down.

units.leftText: Boaz took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, “Sit down here,” and they sat down.
units.rightText: And he took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, Sit ye down here. And they sat down.

units.leftText: He said to the near kinsman, “Naomi, who has come back out of the country of Moab, is selling the parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.
units.rightText: And he said unto the near kinsman, Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth the parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s:

units.leftText: I thought I should tell you, saying, ‘Buy it before those who sit here, and before the elders of my people.’ If you will redeem it, redeem it; but if you will not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know. For there is no one to redeem it besides you; and I am after you.”
units.rightText: and I thought to disclose it unto thee, saying, Buy it before them that sit here, and before the elders of my people. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it: but if thou wilt not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know; for there is none to redeem it besides thee; and I am after thee. And he said, I will redeem it.

units.leftText: Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the field from the hand of Naomi, you must buy it also from Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance.”
units.rightText: Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.

units.leftText: The near kinsman said, “I can’t redeem it for myself, lest I endanger my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption for yourself; for I can’t redeem it.”
units.rightText: And the near kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: take thou my right of redemption on thee; for I cannot redeem it.

units.leftText: Now this was the custom in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning exchanging, to confirm all things: a man took off his sandal, and gave it to his neighbor; and this was the way of formalizing transactions in Israel.
units.rightText: Now this was the custom in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning exchanging, to confirm all things: a man drew off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbor; and this was the manner of attestation in Israel.

units.leftText: So the near kinsman said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself,” then he took off his sandal.
units.rightText: So the near kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy it for thyself. And he drew off his shoe.

units.leftText: Boaz said to the elders and to all the people, “You are witnesses today, that I have bought all that was Elimelech’s, and all that was Chilion’s and Mahlon’s, from the hand of Naomi.
units.rightText: And Boaz said unto the elders, and unto all the people, Ye are witnesses this day, that I have bought all that was Elimelech’s, and all that was Chilion’s and Mahlon’s, of the hand of Naomi.

units.leftText: Moreover, Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, I have purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance, that the name of the dead may not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses today.”
units.rightText: Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place: ye are witnesses this day.

units.leftText: All the people who were in the gate, and the elders, said, “We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman who has come into your house like Rachel and like Leah, which both built the house of Israel; and treat you worthily in Ephrathah, and be famous in Bethlehem.
units.rightText: And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said, We are witnesses. Jehovah make the woman that is come into thy house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel: and do thou worthily in Ephrathah, and be famous in Beth-lehem:

units.leftText: Let your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, of the offspring which the LORD will give you by this young woman.”
units.rightText: and let thy house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah, of the seed which Jehovah shall give thee of this young woman.

units.leftText: So Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife; and he went in to her, and the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she bore a son.
units.rightText: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife; and he went in unto her, and Jehovah gave her conception, and she bare a son.

units.leftText: The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you today without a near kinsman. Let his name be famous in Israel.
units.rightText: And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed be Jehovah, who hath not left thee this day without a near kinsman; and let his name be famous in Israel.

units.leftText: He shall be to you a restorer of life and sustain you in your old age; for your daughter-in-law, who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons, has given birth to him.”
units.rightText: And he shall be unto thee a restorer of life, and a nourisher of thine old age, for thy daughter-in-law, who loveth thee, who is better to thee than seven sons, hath borne him.

units.leftText: Naomi took the child, laid him in her bosom, and became nurse to him.
units.rightText: And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it.

units.leftText: The women, her neighbors, gave him a name, saying, “A son is born to Naomi”. They named him Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
units.rightText: And the women her neighbors gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

units.leftText: Now this is the history of the generations of Perez: Perez became the father of Hezron,
units.rightText: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez begat Hezron,

units.leftText: and Hezron became the father of Ram, and Ram became the father of Amminadab,
units.rightText: and Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab,

units.leftText: and Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon became the father of Salmon,
units.rightText: and Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon,

units.leftText: and Salmon became the father of Boaz, and Boaz became the father of Obed,
units.rightText: and Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,

units.leftText: and Obed became the father of Jesse, and Jesse became the father of David.
units.rightText: and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.
